conceptZh: 豬探長用大放大鏡找蜜蜂，蜂字的筆畫從邊邊探頭又躲開，最後被他一口氣「抓到」。
object: a detective pig with an oversized magnifying glass
morph: strokes of 蜂 sneak in from edges and dodge the pig's lens until they settle
creativeAngle: 捉迷藏：放大鏡把筆畫放大，筆畫一躲就縮小。

Audio: a warm off-screen voice in clear Taiwanese Mandarin reads exactly "蜂、蜂、蜜蜂" (ㄈㄥ、ㄈㄥ、ㄇㄧˋ ㄈㄥ), slowly and distinctly with clear tones, a short pause between the two single utterances, and stops after the word; no other speech, no subtitles, no vocabulary text. Final 3 seconds (5-8s): the glyph 蜂 is perfectly still and fully readable while the lead keeps a small joyful motion away from the strokes. Bright but not neon palette, no watermark, no flashing, no other writing.

conceptZh: 大怪獸想吃掛在高處的蜂巢，把六角蜂巢積木一塊塊疊成搖搖晃晃的高塔，踮腳放上最後一小塊，塔整個嘩啦倒下，碎塊堆成蜂字，把牠埋到只剩眼睛，一隻小蜜蜂從堆裡嗡嗡飛出來停在牠的角上。
object: a huge round fuzzy one-horned cartoon monster stacking chunky hexagonal honeycomb blocks into a wobbling tower to reach a dripping honeycomb hanging from a branch at the top of frame
morph: the tower topples and the tumbling honeycomb blocks land in a heap that settles as the solid strokes of 蜂: the left blocks stack into 虫, the right blocks fall into 夆 (夂 on top, 丰 below), with the monster buried underneath and only its eyes showing
creativeAngle: 前一版是豬探長找筆畫的躲貓貓，這版改成完全不同的「疊高再倒塌」實體笑料：怪獸的笨拙變成塔越疊越歪的來源，倒塌本身直接把積木撞成蜂字，最後鑽出來的小蜜蜂正好對上「蜜蜂」這個詞，聽到的和看到的是同一件事。
promptEn:
An 8-second 2D cartoon clip on a pale butter-cream background. The only text ever on screen is the single Traditional Chinese glyph 蜂, built from solid deep honey-orange strokes, centered, uncropped, about 70% of frame height with generous margins, correctly structured: 虫 on the left, 夆 on the right with 夂 above and 丰 below.

Lead: a huge round fuzzy mint-green cartoon monster with one stubby horn and a goofy grin, clumsy and eager, who knocks things over just by turning around. Only three things on screen: the monster, a pile of chunky hexagonal honeycomb blocks, and a dripping golden honeycomb hanging from a branch at the top of frame.

0-1.5s: the monster stares up at the honeycomb, licks its lips, reaches, and its paw falls far short. It grabs a honeycomb block and slams it down at center. The first 蜂 is spoken as that first block thumps into place and the build begins.

1.5-3.5s: fast stacking. Block, block, block, the tower rising crookedly; the monster climbs onto it, balancing on tiptoe, arms out, the tower swaying wider with every piece. Its tail swipes and knocks a block off, so it stacks it back on even more crooked.

3.5-4.5s: one tiny last block, the size of a sugar cube, placed on the very top. Frozen beat, everything still, the monster's grin stretching. Then the whole tower goes over with a big cartoon tumble. The second 蜂 is spoken as the falling blocks crash down and shake into the glyph 蜂: the left blocks stacking into 虫, the right blocks settling into 夆 with squash-and-stretch and a satisfying click, the monster buried beneath the heap with only two wide eyes poking out.

4.5-5.5s: the pile stops wobbling. 蜜蜂 is spoken exactly as a chubby striped toy bee with round glassy wings buzzes up out of the heap, loops once, and lands on the tip of the monster's horn beside the glyph, never touching the strokes.

5-8s: final hold. The glyph 蜂 stays perfectly still, fully readable, centered. Below the right edge the monster's eyes blink, it wiggles its fuzzy ears, and one happy paw pops out of the pile to give a little wave while the bee bobs on its horn.

Audio: a warm, friendly off-screen voice in clear Taiwanese Mandarin reads exactly 蜂、蜂、蜜蜂 (ㄈㄥ、ㄈㄥ、ㄇㄧˋ ㄈㄥ), slowly and distinctly with clear tones, a short pause between the two single syllables, and stops after the word. Soft wooden block clunks, one cartoon crash and a tiny buzz, all quieter than the voice. No other speech, no subtitles, no vocabulary text, no watermark, no flashing, no other writing. Bright but not neon palette, no white blowouts, no dark grading.
